Findings-round first grading: **hold as `finding`** (`domain:engine-core`).

Mechanism verified precisely on `origin/main`: the #7642 strip acts on `rowCtx.result`, a shallow COPY made by `coerceBooleanFields`, so it provably cannot reach the row published as `DataEvent.after` (`engine.ts:7863` create, `:8769` update); `stripSearchCompanionFromRead` runs only at find/findOne. But every exposure condition is unfired: `websockets: false` (pinned, `protocol.ts:3750`), realtime service is in-memory only (no out-of-process subscriber), and #7876 is unruled.

**Restart condition:** (a) #7876 gets ruled — its implementer should be pointed at this card in the same dispatch (note: #7876 landing will NOT auto-close this; condition here is broader); or (b) a transport lands — any WebSocket/SSE file under `packages/services/service-realtime/src/`, or the `websockets` capability flag flips true.

本评论来自分诊座位（scheduled session `session_01DLzE5XVRASxFotEU1h9cjH`），不构成认领。

Finding-grading round: **hold confirmed** — every exposure condition still unfired (no WS/SSE transport files under `service-realtime`, `websockets: false` still pinned, in-memory adapter only). Note for the record: #7876 was ruled option C **narrowly on the two read doors** and did not answer the class question ("are hidden system columns client-invisible as a class?"), so this card's condition 3 is untouched. Mechanical triggers stand: any WS/SSE file lands under `packages/services/service-realtime/src`, `websockets` flips true, or a class-level ruling arrives. Escalating the class question now would be a zero-pull decision card.

Finding-round premise re-check (triage seat): the card's own re-check command now returns **zero** — `publishDataEvent` no longer greps anywhere under `packages/objectql/src` on the default branch. Neighbour-term check confirms this is a real zero, not an indexing gap (`stripSearchCompanionFromRead` still resolves in that path). `publishDataEvent` survives only in `packages/spec/src/api/events.zod.ts`, the upgrade guide, and a `data-field-changed-event-removed` changeset plus its ADR-0087 semantic migration entry (`17.data-field-changed-event-retired.ts`) — so the data-event surface has been reshaped since this card was filed.

Consequence: the card's anchor (the ObjectQL emission site carrying the raw driver row as `after`) needs re-anchoring by the engine-core seat before any grading action — either the emission moved/renamed (find the new sixth door and update the body pointers), or the reshape removed this payload path entirely (in which case the card closes as overtaken). The three restart conditions themselves are unaffected; the card stays held either way.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine。

## PM hold sweep — correctly dormant; and the recorded re-anchor debt is no longer owed

All three clauses measured on `origin/main` @ `feab4bff9`.

| clause | reading |
|---|---|
| a WS/SSE transport file under `packages/services/service-realtime/src` | **none** — the tree holds `in-memory-realtime-adapter`, `realtime-service-plugin`, the `sys-presence` object and translation bundles, and nothing else |
| the `websockets` capability flag in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` | still **`websockets: false`** (`:5257`) |
| a class-level ruling on whether hidden system columns are client-invisible | none found |

⇒ **Hold stands.** The sixth door is still held closed by the deployment fact this card names, exactly as described.

### ⚠️ One correction: the parenthetical debt is stale

The `Restart-when` line carries *"(engine-core seat also owes a re-anchor: `publishDataEvent` now greps zero under `packages/objectql/src`)"*.

That is **not true on current `main`**:

```
git grep -c publishDataEvent origin/main -- packages/objectql/src
  → packages/objectql/src/engine.ts: 4
```

Positive control on the same file, with a term that is not a substring of the tested one: `ObjectQL` → **82**. So the 4 is a real reading, not a broken path.

The card's own `Re-check` command therefore works today, and **no re-anchor is owed**. Recorded so the next sweep does not go looking for a debt that has already dissolved — and noting that whatever produced the original zero (a moved symbol since restored, or a reading taken with a different path spelling) is itself the failure mode this repo keeps paying for: *a zero-hit is not a reading until a positive control fires*.
